mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.1% indicates aggressive monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase above 5.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) growth above 10% YoY indicate robust consumer demand, driving corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when HOUST and RSAFS both exceed 10% YoY growth.

mechanism_narrative: Manufacturing slowdown regime (INDPRO growth below 0.5% monthly) reduces industrial output and corporate margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO growth is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth above 2% (GDPC1) indicates expanding economic activity, increasing corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of quarters when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI increase above 0.5% (CPIAUCSL) signals accelerating inflation, triggering central bank tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises above 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous employment decline (PAYEMS growth < 0.2%) and unemployment rise (UNRATE > 5.0%) indicate labor market contraction, reducing consumer spending and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS growth is below 0.2% and UNRATE exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: High interest rate regime (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) increases discount rates and reduces leverage, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0%.
